dok_rationale: Part (c) weighs competing claims using the day's numerical or graphical evidence and explains a limitation or consequence; the judgment requires linked reasoning beyond a calculation.
stem: Suppose a dispatcher models delivery time using eight equally likely outcomes for each route, shown in the dotplots. An analyst reports that both routes have mean 30 minutes, with $\sigma_A=3$ minutes and $\sigma_B=12$ minutes.\par\smallskip The dispatcher says, \emph{The routes have the same mean, so it does not matter which one a customer gets.} A customer has 40 minutes before an appointment and places a high cost on being late.\par For the eight outcomes, the sums of squared distances from 30 are 72 for Route A and 1,152 for Route B.
first_take: Which route would you assign to this customer? Cite one number or dotplot feature.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Count the outcomes longer than 40 minutes for each route.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the given sums of squared distances to verify both population standard deviations. Interpret what one of them means in minutes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Which route fits this customer's priority? Use both standard deviations and the chance of exceeding 40 minutes. Explain why the dispatcher's mean-only comparison can mislead this customer. Write 3--4 sentences.

answers.a: Route A has no outcomes longer than 40 minutes. Route B has two: 42 and 50 minutes.
answers.b: $\sigma_A=\sqrt{72/8}=3$ minutes; $\sigma_B=\sqrt{1152/8}=12$ minutes. Route A's modeled delivery times typically differ from their 30-minute mean by about 3 minutes.
answers.c: Choose Route A: its standard deviation is 3 minutes rather than 12, so its modeled times vary less around the same 30-minute mean. No A outcome exceeds 40 minutes, compared with $2/8=25\%$ for B. Equal means do not imply equal chances of being late, so the dispatcher's comparison hides the difference this customer cares about. This conclusion uses the eight equally likely outcomes in the stated model.

expectedElements.description: Chooses A using standard deviations 3 versus 12 minutes
Connects 0/8 versus 2/8 above 40 to the customer's deadline
Explains that equal means do not imply equal variability or late risk

scoringGuide.E: Includes all three required reasoning elements above, with correct contextual evidence.
scoringGuide.P: Includes at least one substantive correct reasoning link above, but omits or misstates another required element.
scoringGuide.I: Includes no substantive correct reasoning link above; an unsupported choice or copied number alone is insufficient.

commonMistakes: Treating standard deviation as minutes added to every delivery
Claiming every Route B time is exactly 12 minutes from its mean
Using equal means alone to infer equal chances of missing the deadline

sentence_frames: Route \blank[0.4in] fits because its SD is \blank[0.5in] minutes and its chance of exceeding 40 minutes is \blank[0.7in].
The equal means describe \blank[1.3in], but they do not show \blank[2.1in].
